== Overview ==
The Kofun was constructed on the tip of a hill projecting westward in the northern region of {{ill|Lake Suwa|ar|بحيرة سوا|arz|بحيره سوا|ceb|Suwa Ko|de|Suwa-See|eo|Suŭa-Lago|es|Lago Suwa|et|Suwa järv|eu|Suwa aintzira|fa|دریاچه سووا|fr|Lac Suwa|id|Danau Suwa|ja|諏訪湖|ko|스와호|lt|Suva (ežeras)|mk|Сува (езеро)|my|ဆုဝကန်|nn|Suwasjøen|pl|Suwa (jezioro)|ro|Lacul Suwa|ru|Сува (озеро)|sr|Језеро Сува|th|ทะเลสาบซูวะ|tr|Suwa Gölü|vi|Hồ Suwa|zh|諏訪湖|zh_yue|諏訪湖|qid=Q1206692|lt=Lake Suwa}}. It is situated near the {{ill|Shimosha Akimiya|ja|諏訪大社下社秋宮}} of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|abstract|Q218813|de|Suwa-Taisha|es|Suwa taisha|eu|Suwa taisha|fa|زیارتگاه بزرگ سووا|fr|Suwa-taisha|hu|Szuva templom|id|Kuil Suwa|it|Santuario di Suwa (Sohonsha)|ja|諏訪大社|ko|스와 대사|lt|Suvos maldykla|pl|Suwa Taisha|ru|Сува-тайся|simple|Suwa-taisha|tr|Suwa-taisha|zh|諏訪大社|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa Taisha}}. The site is within the shrine's property, and parts of the mound (especially the eastern side) have been eroded by surrounding developments. The {{ill|Aozuka Shrine|ja|青塚社}}, a subsidiary shrine of Suwa Taisha, is located in the western constriction area of the mound.

The kofun is keyhole-shaped with its front part oriented to the north-northwest. It is the only keyhole-shaped Kofun in the Suwa region and belongs to the late phase of this style. {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|qid=Q11394845}} have been discovered on the mound's surface, making it the only example in the Suwa region where haniwa have been found. Historical records from the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} mention the discovery of human-shaped haniwa, which were later reburied, though recent investigations have found no items other than cylindrical haniwa. 

The burial facility is a {{ill|Corridor-Style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|ko|굴식 돌방무덤|zh|橫穴式石室|qid=Q11543435}} exposed and open on the western constriction area of the rear mound, approximately five meters above the base level. The chamber is constructed with natural {{ill|Andesite|af|Andesiet|an|Andesita|ar|أنديزيت|az|Andezit|be|Андэзіт|bg|Андезит|bn|অ্যান্ডিসাইট|ca|Andesita|cs|Andezit|da|Andesit|de|Andesit|el|Ανδεσίτης|eo|Andezito|es|Andesita|et|Andesiit|eu|Andesita|fa|آندزیت|fi|Andesiitti|fr|Andésite|ga|Aindéisít|gl|Andesita|he|אנדזיט|hi|एंडेसाइट|hr|Andezit|hsb|Andezit|hu|Andezit|hy|Անդեզիտ|id|Andesit|is|Andesít|it|Andesite|ja|安山岩|jv|Andhésit|ka|ანდეზიტი|kk|Андезит|kn|ಆಂಡಿಸೈಟ್|ko|안산암|kw|Andesit|ky|Андезит|lt|Andezitas|mk|Андезит|nds|Andesit|nl|Andesiet|nn|Andesitt|no|Andesitt|oc|Andesita|pl|Andezyt|pt|Andesito|ro|Andezit|ru|Андезит|sh|Andezit|simple|Andesite|sk|Andezit|sl|Andezit|sr|Андезит|su|Andésit|sv|Andesit|tg|Андезит|tl|Andesita|tr|Andezit|uk|Андезит|uz|Andezit|vi|Andesit|wuu|安山岩|zh|安山岩|qid=Q181908|lt=andesite}} stones in a random stone masonry style. It measures 5.5 meters in total length. Although the corridor leading to the chamber has been destroyed, it is presumed to have been a double-chambered type. Few burial goods from the chamber are known.

The Aozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the late 6th century. Scholars suggest links to the {{ill|Kanasashi clan|ja|金刺氏}}, the ritualist family of Suwa Taisha's Shimosha, and connections with other keyhole-shaped Kofuns distributed along the {{ill|Tenryū River|arz|نهر تينريو|ceb|Tenryū-gawa (suba sa Hapon)|de|Tenryū (Fluss)|eu|Tenryū ibaia|fa|رود تنریو|fr|Tenryū-gawa|id|Sungai Tenryū|ja|天竜川|ko|덴류강|my|တန်းရူးမြစ်|no|Tenryu (elv)|ru|Тенрю (река)|tg|Тенрю (дарё)|tr|Tenryū Nehri|zh|天龍川|qid=Q13667|lt=Tenryu River}}. This makes the mound an important archaeological site for studying the political landscape of ancient Suwa.

The Kofun was Historic Site1 as a Nagano Prefecture historic site in 1965.

== Mound ==
The mound's area are as follows:
* Mound length: 57 meters
* Rear part:
''' Diameter: 34 meters (estimated reconstruction)
''' Height: 8.1 meters
* Front part:
''' Width: 40 meters (estimated reconstruction)
''' Height: 8 meters

According to the site's intypeation board, the primary axis length is 67 meters, the rear part's diameter is 33.4 meters, and the front part's width is 42.8 meters.
